newsitem.title: USA: NYS Senate unveils big school property tax relief.
newsitem.headline: NYS Senate unveils big school property tax relief.

text.p: The New York State Senate Majority Leader on Tuesday unveiled a five-year plan to cut school property taxes by nearly $3 billion, saying it combined the best elements of the Senate's and governor's proposals.
The plan would give more state aid to school districts that voluntarily froze property taxes, a suggestion Gov. George Pataki put forward in the preliminary budget he proposed for fiscal 1998.

Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, said the plan would give school districts an extra three percent of state aid in return for capping their property taxes. The program would save over $1.2 billion in school taxes when fully put in place in 2001 to 2002.
"This bill combines the strongest elements of the Senate's school property tax reform plan and Gov Pataki's School Tax Relief proposal," said Bruno, in prepared remarks.

The Senate sought to avoid a problem the governor's plan encountered, by immediately making eligible cooperative apartments, as well as condominiums and one- to three-family homes. Pataki in mid-February widened his program to include co-ops--most of which are in New York City--after criticism.

Bruno's program would result in a 27 percent cut in school taxes for the owner of a median-priced home in each county. Schools that held down administrative costs as a percentage of their overall budget would get extra funds. Schools also would get access to pooled financing and construction management services from the state Dormitory Authority. And school districts throughout the state would have to submit their budgets to voters on the third Tuesday in May.
